method.reviewer: Independent Codex text review; no new local or external LLM-judge call
method.scope: Intrinsic grammar, coherence, scientific plausibility and unsupported claims. This is a reasoned screening pass, not factual certification or peer review.
method.acceptance_rule: accepted=true only for decision=accepted. Uncertain candidates are withheld from automatic anchor selection. Accepted candidates may retain explicitly nonblocking scope/precision notes.
method.topic_note: Some supplied domain labels differ from the actual prose subject (notably quantum decoherence under hidden-ml and federated learning under hidden-quantum). Their relation to a target was not used to judge intrinsic quality.
method.comparison_note: Each actual candidate was read; recurring terminology was not used as a blanket rejection. In particular, effective reduced-state mixtures are distinguished from objective collapse, and conditional partial-failure availability is distinguished from an all-partitions guarantee.

reasons: Grammar: "causes information leak" needs "causes information to leak" or "causes information leakage".
Scientific setup: calling the decohering subsystem "closed" while letting information escape into an environment confuses closed-system unitary evolution with an open subsystem.

"Effectively collapsing ... into a classical probability distribution" is not adequately qualified as reduced-system interference suppression. Effective-collapse shorthand can be defensible, but this paragraph never identifies a reduced state or distinguishes it from physical outcome selection.

Scientific setup: a quantum subsystem coupled to and leaking information into its environment is open; "a closed system interacts with its surrounding environment" is contradictory in the quantum-dynamical sense used here.

"Transforming a coherent superposition into a classical mixture" omits the reduced-state/effective-description qualification. This candidate does NOT explicitly claim selection of a measurement outcome; the rejection is for the closed/open confusion and an unqualified classical-mixture description, not for merely discussing decoherence.
notes: The prose is otherwise grammatical. A corrected account could describe environmental entanglement and an approximately diagonal reduced density matrix.

reasons: Grammar: "causes information leak" is malformed; use "causes information to leak".
The purported "closed system" simultaneously exchanges information with an environment, confusing closed combined dynamics with open-subsystem dynamics.
The effective-collapse/classical-distribution claim needs an explicit reduced-system qualification; decoherence alone does not establish physical collapse or a singled-out result.
Coherent, grammatical account of quorum commitment, log agreement and leader/log management in replicated databases.
No explicit promise of availability in every partition is made; availability under some partial failures is compatible with a connected operational majority.
notes: "High availability" needs the connected-majority/failure-model qualification in a precise exposition. Log agreement is necessary, but is not by itself the complete linearizability argument or a read-path specification.

reasons: Readable description of a leader/quorum log protocol and failover, with term/index safeguards against incompatible committed histories.
No concrete grammatical failure or unsupported empirical result is present.
notes: Interpret "without losing data" as preserving committed entries; uncommitted proposals may be discarded. A precise version should say "committed data" and distinguish safety from eventual election progress.

reasons: The quorum/majority, term-number and log-replication explanation is scientifically plausible as a high-level crash-fault consensus summary.
It does not state that majority acknowledgments alone are the entire safety mechanism; the last sentence explicitly adds term/log safeguards.
notes: Agreement can remain safe during a partition while progress stops; the opening should not be read as guaranteed availability. Exact voting, log-freshness and commitment rules are omitted, as expected in a short overview.

reasons: Corrupted terminology: "histone ortranslational modifications" is not a valid description; the intended term is presumably post-translational histone modifications.
"Target proteins or modified modifications" is semantically broken, and "specific gene genes" duplicates a word.
"Sequenced and mapped to map" is clumsy repetition. ChIP enrichment is also overstated as a comprehensive regulatory architecture rather than binding/mark evidence with limits.
Grammar artifact: "specific factor factors" duplicates a word.
Sequencing antibody-enriched material maps occupancy or selected histone-mark enrichment; it does not automatically reveal the precise locations of every enhancer and promoter.

Binding plus transcriptomic profiles can support regulatory hypotheses, but the paragraph overstates inference of how chromatin states drive expression without explaining a causal design or validation.
The crosslinked ChIP-seq workflow is plausible and the paragraph is grammatical.

However, protein occupancy plus accessibility profiles is promoted to "a comprehensive understanding" of how architecture influences expression, without functional or causal evidence. This is too broad to approve unchanged as a scientifically careful anchor.

This is not an assertion that combining these assays is useless, nor the same explicit "directly determines causality" wording seen elsewhere; the remaining problem is the unqualified mechanistic/completeness claim.
notes: Replace the final claim with identifying candidate regulatory associations/hypotheses, or specify orthogonal functional validation.

reasons: Definition error: radiative forcing is a change in net radiative flux including shortwave and longwave radiation, not just "net solar radiation".
Grammar artifact: "water water vapor shifts" duplicates a word.
The first sentence compares solar energy at the surface with energy emitted to space, mixing different budget boundaries. That is not a definition of radiative forcing.
Forcing is the imposed change in the relevant net radiative flux, not the entire evolving energy imbalance after feedbacks.
"Cloud vapor changes" conflates clouds (condensed water/ice) with water vapor; cloud and water-vapor feedbacks should be named separately.
Definition error: the forcing flux includes solar/shortwave and thermal/longwave components; "net solar radiation" excludes the greenhouse longwave contribution.
The duplicated "water water" is a clear wording artifact.
Coherent description of a common centrally aggregated federated-learning setup, client heterogeneity and communication costs.
The privacy sentence correctly warns that sharing updates can expose information through inversion attacks; it does not equate keeping raw data local with a privacy guarantee.
notes: This is a central-server variant, not a description of every possible federated architecture. Its actual subject is machine learning, despite the supplied case topic label; topic alignment was deliberately not scored.

reasons: Grammatical and scientifically plausible summary of client-side learning and server-side parameter-update aggregation.
It explicitly retains a privacy-risk qualification rather than claiming that local raw-data retention prevents leakage.
notes: "Gradient attacks" is underspecified; gradient reconstruction/inversion or membership inference would be clearer. This imprecision is not a concrete false claim. Actual subject: federated learning.

reasons: "Instead of aggregating information centrally" conflicts with the same sentence sending information to a central server "for aggregation". It presumably means avoiding centralization of raw data, but that distinction is absent.

The passage also presents sending parameter gradients as the universal update form, while common federated local-training protocols send parameter/model differences. Gradient-sharing is possible, so this is an underspecified variant rather than an intrinsically impossible algorithm.
notes: Clarify "without centralizing raw training data" and name a federated-SGD variant or say "model updates" before approval.

reasons: Readable and plausible account of coupled pose/map estimation, noisy measurements and loop closure for drift correction.
"Often employ recursive filters" correctly leaves room for graph/optimization-based approaches rather than defining all SLAM as filtering.
notes: Loop closure is a common consistency aid, not an unconditional guarantee that every map is globally correct. Correct association and observability assumptions remain implicit.

reasons: The ending "local-term perceptual noise" contains a malformed, undefined compound and obscures the intended meaning.
Otherwise the paragraph is nearly a coherent filtering/loop-closure summary, but this wording artifact prevents approval as polished text.
notes: Replace with "local perceptual noise" or "short-term perceptual noise" as intended.

reasons: Grammatical, but it defines the process as relying on recursive filtering even though optimization/smoothing-based SLAM is a major alternative.

"Robust algorithms must employ loop closure" is too categorical, and detecting a loop does not by itself ensure global consistency; sensing, data association and other absolute/relative constraints matter.
notes: Qualify the scope as a filtering-based approach and loop closure as one common correction mechanism.

reasons: The paragraph coherently describes activity-dependent efficacy changes, receptor trafficking and persistent potentiation.
Distinguishing stable modifications from transient fluctuations is a sensible evaluation aim, and no specific corrupted wording or invented quantitative result appears.
notes: "Sensitivity of the cell" is broad; postsynaptic responsiveness at the affected synapse would be more precise. The summary does not cover every form of plasticity.

reasons: Broken sentence boundary: "the sensitivity of the cell to Long-term potentiation represents" merges two sentences into an ungrammatical construction.
The resulting text no longer states a coherent relation between receptor trafficking and potentiation.

The NMDA-receptor coincidence description is scientifically plausible: glutamate binding and postsynaptic depolarization permit calcium-dependent signaling that can modify glutamate-receptor expression/trafficking.
The prose is grammatical, and "often" appropriately avoids treating this as every form of synaptic plasticity.
notes: Persistence measurements alone do not prove a structural rather than functional mechanism. If the final sentence is intended as an experimental recipe for structural attribution, structural readouts would also be needed.

reasons: The free-energy/nucleation overview is broadly plausible, but "local fluctuations must propagate to reach global equilibrium" is not a clear account of nucleation and growth. Critical nuclei overcoming a free-energy barrier and subsequent interface growth are conflated with propagation of fluctuations.

The inference from grain-boundary evolution to how disorder controls stability/mechanical response is presented without a measurement/model connection; it needs a specified material/transformation or narrower wording.
notes: This is a precision/unsupported-mechanism concern, not a claim that grain boundaries cannot affect transformations.

reasons: A coherent, grammatical introductory description of structural solid-state transformations, free-energy driving, nucleation/growth and diffraction/thermal-expansion measurements.
No duplicated tokens, malformed sentence or invented measurement is present.
notes: The scope should be structural first-order transformations: not every transition has nucleation/growth kinetics. At changing pressure, the thermodynamic discussion should explicitly include pressure-volume/enthalpic contributions rather than only internal energy and entropy.

reasons: The clause "local fluctuations must overcome to reach global equilibrium" lacks the object of "overcome"; an activation/free-energy barrier is presumably missing.
This omission also removes the physical mechanism the sentence is meant to explain.
Clear wording artifact: "frequent frequency elections".

The unconditional framing of maintaining safety "without sacrificing availability" in the same paragraph as network partitions is misleading for Raft/Paxos. Availability requires a communicating operational quorum; safety does not imply progress during arbitrary partitions.
Clear duplicated wording: "frequent frequency elections".
Subject/verb disagreement: "rapid state transitions is critical" should be "are critical".
The safety/availability tradeoff is now acknowledged, but it does not repair those grammar defects.
The paragraph is grammatical and correctly emphasizes failure testing, but it asks for recovery of "consistency" when a quorum is unreachable or inconsistent.

For crash-fault quorum protocols, quorum loss should stop progress while preserving the safety of committed history; recovery may mean replica catch-up, not regaining a safety property that was lost. If inconsistent means Byzantine behavior, that needs a different explicit fault model.
The intended meaning is ambiguous rather than demonstrably impossible, so this is withheld pending clarification rather than labeled a clear factual falsehood.
notes: Use "resume progress and catch up lagging replicas after quorum connectivity returns while preserving committed-history safety" if that is the intended test.

reasons: A grammatical and plausible introductory account of line fingerprints, Doppler shifts, thermal/pressure-related broadening and instrumental corrections.
Line-profile modeling can inform source temperature, pressure and radial velocity; no specific numerical inference or discovery is fabricated.
notes: These quantities are not generally uniquely recoverable from a width/shift alone: broadening components and line formation require models and additional diagnostics. Instrumental correction also does not by itself separate interstellar absorption from source features.

reasons: Coherent description of spectroscopy using line shifts/intensities and atomic modeling to infer abundances, temperatures and radial velocities.
It avoids a concrete unsupported quantitative claim and has no visible grammar or coherence defect.
notes: The galaxy-evolution conclusion is broad motivation, not evidence that a particular evolutionary model was confirmed.

reasons: Missing noun: "interaction of electromagnetic with matter" needs electromagnetic radiation/fields.
Malformed construction: "to account between physical signals from instrumental noise"; it should distinguish signals from noise or account for instrumental effects.
"The evolution across the universe" leaves the object of evolution unspecified, and "individual atmospheres" is an unclear replacement for individual stars in this context.
